addendum: F16 (review response: small adversarial experiment; public vs keyed codeword assignment)
status: supplementary analysis after the locked test; it does not change H1-H4 or their verdicts
question: Can an attacker who knows the public BCH(32,16) codebook, the decoding rule and a target user's public ID make the calibrated attribution rule (method C) accept a forged watermark as that user, and does a secret keyed assignment of IDs to codewords prevent it without lowering legitimate attribution?

attacker_has: the WAM embedder (same checkpoint wam_coco; worst case)
the public BCH(32,16) codebook and the soft decoding rule
the public 16-bit ID of the target registered user

goals.targeted: the detector accepts the forged region as the target user T
goals.untargeted: the detector accepts the forged region as any registered user (framing)

not_covered: copy or replay of a genuine watermark (any key-based assignment is replayable)
attacks that train a surrogate decoder

schemes.PUB: codeword index = ID (the assignment used in V3/V4: registered IDs are the codeword indices of the operational registry)
schemes.KEY: codeword index = pi_K(ID), pi_K a secret uniformly random permutation of {0..65535}; the decoder maps the decoded index c back to pi_K^-1(c) and applies the same registry check and threshold. In this experiment pi_K is numpy.random.default_rng(key_seed).permutation(65536); in practice a keyed pseudo-random permutation (e.g. format-preserving encryption)

data.images: reserve COCO val2017 4,500-4,999 (500 images; already used by E3, E4 and R4)

registry.source: operational registry of V3/V4 (seed 20261100, N = 1,000 BCH16 IDs), checked against reports/analysis/v3_thresholds.json

acceptance.rule: method C as locked: decoded codeword by soft correlation over the full codebook; accept if the decoded ID is registered and max correlation > tau_C

scenes.layout: WAM Sec. 5.5 checkerboard, k = 5 messages per image (10% squares), regions assigned to messages by the WAM largest-overlap rule (as V4)
scenes.targets: per image 5 distinct target IDs drawn without replacement from the registry, seed 20261108

embeddings.E_pub: bch[T] for each target: legitimate embedding under PUB, and the attacker's forgery under both schemes (without K the attacker can only use the public codeword of T)
embeddings.E_key: bch[pi_K0(T)]: legitimate embedding under KEY with the primary key K0 (key_seed 20261109)

scenes.eligibility: a message counts only if its visible area is at least 1,000 pixels (as V4)

measures.R_legit_PUB: share of eligible target slots in E_pub with a region assigned to the slot that decodes to codeword T with score > tau_C
measures.R_legit_KEY: the same in E_key with codeword pi_K0(T)
measures.F_target_PUB: equals R_legit_PUB (the forgery and the legitimate embedding are the same codeword)
measures.F_target_KEY: share of eligible slots in E_pub with a region assigned to the slot whose decoded ID pi_K0^-1(c) equals T and score > tau_C
measures.F_untarget_KEY: share of eligible slots in E_pub with a region assigned to the slot whose decoded ID pi_K^-1(c) is registered and score > tau_C; computed for the primary key K0 and for 1,000 random keys (seeds 20262000-20262999) from the same decoded indices and scores (decoding does not depend on K)
measures.F_untarget_expected: N / 65,536 x share of E_pub slots decoded to T with score > tau_C (uniform random permutation)

decision_supplementary.condition: hflip_contrast1.5 (the H1 decision condition); none is reported with the same rules
decision_supplementary.D1_targeted: keyed assignment prevents targeted forgery if the 98.75% one-sided Clopper-Pearson upper bound of F_target_KEY is below the 98.75% one-sided lower bound of F_target_PUB
decision_supplementary.D2_legit: keyed assignment keeps legitimate attribution if the 98.75% image-paired bootstrap interval (10,000 repeats, seed 20261006) of R_legit_KEY - R_legit_PUB lies inside +-0.02
decision_supplementary.D3_untargeted: reported, not decided: F_untarget_KEY (K0 and median, 5-95% over 1,000 keys) against the expected value and against the 1% false attribution target

reporting: results go to reports/analysis/review_F16_summary.json and are reported as a supplementary adversarial analysis in the discussion and limitations; whatever the outcome, the numbers are reported as measured
script: scripts/verify/review_f16.py (verifies this plan's sha256, the base protocol, wam_coco and the reserve image list before running and stops on any mismatch)
